evidence: Design reasoning holds for every floor case. test.sh:68-70,123-125 zero a missing/unstartable app; gates are binary all_pass and score.py:41,48 zero the reward when either gate is 0. gates/render/judge.toml:26-33 fails a blank page, static mock, generic error, private data before sign-in, accepted wrong password or failed gwen sign-in; gates/constraints/judge.toml:26-36 requires gwen's post 'Gate check JUDGE-G1' in M-11 to survive reload and appear for harriet in a separate context, so a static/mock/seed-copy/keyword-stuffed page or a submission refusing every action scores 0 (no CDN/off-origin penalty: render prompt.md:12-13, constraints prompt.md:13-14). Each scored prompt repeats the global gate (functional prompt.md:11-19, polish prompt.md:10-17, visual prompt.md:18-25) and the functional floor (scoring.toml:10-11, functional > 0.05; score.py:47-48) stops a gate-passing shell farming polish/visual. Worst near-shell case: a server-backed generic message board passing both gates but with no walls/retention/holds; its only plausible functional credit is 'persistence' (weight 2.0 of 42.0, functional/judge.toml:32-35,268-280, which grades only durability), giving 2/42 = 0.0476 < 0.05, so reward is 0; other criteria need real behaviour plus positive controls and replays (prompt.md:23-50). Conforming alternative: gate steps (sign-in, wrong-password refusal, post persists and is shared) are core public product behaviour with no prescribed routes, so a valid app is not floored. Risk=true because this is reasoned only: raw-evidence-index.json scope states reward discrimination/ranking runs and a full configured grading run on these bytes are absent, so no weak/shell app has been measured; the persistence-only margin under the floor (0.0476 vs 0.05) is thin.
